title: Grateful Dead Live at L'Olympia on 1972-05-04
source: SBD -> (16 Track) Master Reel -> Dat D

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard recording of a high‑energy 1972 Paris show highlighted by a soaring Dark Star and a pristine Sugar Magnolia.
ai_review.review: The Charlie Miller transfer delivers crystal‑clear board sound that captures the band at one of their creative peaks.  Reviewers rave about the tight, jazz‑laden Dark Star, a monster Good Lovin' and an unforgettable Pigpen‑driven Sugar Magnolia, while noting only a few minor setlist dips.  Overall the performance is described as “smoking,” “tight,” and “magical.”

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 detailed reviews uniformly give 5‑star ratings, praising both the musical performance (70% weight) and the flawless soundboard mix (30% weight).  No significant criticisms were found.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Multiple reviewers call the mix “clean,” “crisp,” and “hardly any crowd noise.”  Charlie Miller’s transfer is repeatedly praised for preserving board clarity without artifacts.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Set 1 builds a classic early‑E72 vibe; Set 2 launches into an extended Dark Star, followed by tight jams and a spectacular second‑half climax with Good Lovin' and Sugar Magnolia.  Transitions are described as seamless and the band re‑tightens after the long improvisations.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly lauded for inspired, jazzy guitar work—especially during Dark Star and Sugar Magnolia (“Jerry's wah,” “blazing”).
band_member_comments.Phil: Mentioned for rumbling bass in the Dark Star space segment and occasional atonal moments; praised as part of the “spacey” vibe.
band_member_comments.Bob: Highlighted for dynamic fills during the drum break in Dark Star and his vocal contribution on Good Lovin'.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s organ chops are called “angelic,” adding a West Coast flavor; noted as a major driver of the show’s rhythm and excitement.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill (Mickey) receives high praise for an exceptional drum solo in the middle of Dark Star, described as “one of Billy's best” and “snappy jazz beat.”
